notes: Interface size: Ctrl+Alt and + or −, or the menu's Interface size, make the browser's own tabs, buttons and menus larger or smaller, from 50% to 200%; Ctrl+Alt+0 goes back to 100%. Ctrl and + or − still zoom the web page. Menus and message boxes follow the window's size. Zooming in makes the window bigger if it would be too small for its layout, as far as the screen allows. The size is kept for this app on this PC.
The menu (⋯) has NorthRay Software's website, which opens the Browser's page on the website in a new tab.
Buttons have Writing Studio's calm look: one style everywhere, a soft frame that lifts when you point at it, and a small icon beside the words where there's room.
Faint text is a little darker in the light theme and a little lighter in the dark one, so it reads easily (WCAG AA), and the light theme's green is deeper for the same reason.
Drag a tab down out of the tab strip to give it a window of its own.
The tabs you had open come back when the browser starts. Their pages open as you go to each tab, so starting stays quick.
Closing a window with five or more tabs asks first.
Each site remembers its own zoom (Ctrl + mouse wheel, or Ctrl and plus or minus). Ctrl+0 puts it back to 100%.
Tabs playing sound show a speaker. Click it to mute the tab, or use Mute tab in the tab's right-click menu.
Rest the pointer on a tab to see its title, its site and a small picture of the page.
Turn the mouse wheel over the tabs to move between them. The tab menu has “Close tabs to the right”, and the tabs' close buttons are bigger and easier to hit.
The address bar shows the site's name clearly with the rest of the address fainter, has a Copy link button, and its right-click menu has Paste and go.
Bookmarks pick up their site's icon once you've visited the site, including bookmarks imported from another browser.
No white flash before a page appears in a dark window, and scrolling glides smoothly.
Reference boards remember the board you were on, and each board's size of pictures (Ctrl + mouse wheel) and where you'd scrolled to.
Fixed: buttons in question boxes didn't respond to clicks when Windows' display scaling was above 100%.

Back up and restore (in the menu): one file holding your bookmarks, reference boards and their pictures, start page notes and background, settings, and (if you choose) your history. Keep it, or take it to another PC: no account, nothing leaves your computer unless you move the file.
Restoring checks the backup first, then restarts the browser to put it in place. Whatever it replaces is kept in a “Before restore” folder, so nothing is lost.
Saved passwords and sign-ins aren't in backups: they stay in the engine's protected store on this PC. The downloads list isn't either, as it points at files on this PC.
Long menus show whole again when they fit on the screen; only very long lists scroll.
The video pop-out takes the shape of the video, and keeps it as you resize it.
Controls on the pop-out while the mouse is over it: back 10 seconds, play or pause, forward 10 seconds.

“Skip ad” appears on the pop-out whenever the site offers to skip an advert (YouTube's button, or a “Skip ad” on other sites), even when the mouse isn't over it, and presses the site's own button for you.
The video pop-out shows just the video: the site's header, menus and everything else on the page are hidden while it's popped out (they come back when it goes back to the tab).

The pop-out's bar (title, back to the tab, close) only appears while the mouse is over the pop-out, on top of the video; drag it to move the pop-out. The frame round the video is now a thin black edge for resizing.

Pop out the video (Alt+P, the menu, the tab's menu or a right-click on the page): the page's video moves into a small window that stays on top of your other apps, with its player's controls and adverts still working. Drag its bar to move it, its edges to resize it; it remembers where you put it.
The pop-out keeps going when an advert ends: its end screen stays, and when the page swaps in the programme's video (or a new player) the pop-out follows it.
Back to the tab (the bar's button, a double-click on the bar, or closing the pop-out) puts the page back where it was, still playing.
Start page: your own background picture (Customise… › Background picture), a clock, and Notes to yourself, kept on this computer as you type.

Weather on the start page, if you want it: Customise… › Weather, type your town, choose it from the list. Today's temperature, high and low, from Open-Meteo (credited on the page); °C or °F. Nothing is fetched until you choose a place.
Make it the default browser: the start page asks once (and the menu has it). NorthRay registers itself with Windows, then opens Windows' Default apps page at it, where only you can make the choice.

Reference boards: right-click a picture on any page and choose “Save picture to a reference board”. Menu › Reference boards shows them in columns, board by board, with the page each came from; make boards for characters, places or covers, rename them, move pictures between them.
Pick a colour from the page (right-click, or the menu): a loupe shows the pixels under the pointer; click to copy the colour (#1F3B2C) and keep it on your board.
“Colours” on a saved picture adds its main colours to the board, as a palette. Click a colour to copy it.

Downloads page (Ctrl+J, the menu, or the new button by the menu): every download with its progress and time left, Pause, Resume and Cancel while it runs, Open and Show in folder when it's done, and Download again if it failed. The list is kept between sessions; a tab closed mid-download finishes it first.

Ads and trackers are blocked: requests to about 120 well-known advertising, tracking and data-collection services are refused when they're on a different site from the page, so pages load faster and fewer companies follow you around. A site's own content is never blocked.
The shield in the address bar shows how many were blocked on the page, and turns blocking off for a site that doesn't work properly (or everywhere).
Google is the default search engine. If you chose another one yourself, it's kept.
History, Bookmarks and Downloads still open when web pages can't be shown.
Messages and questions (“Delete this?”, “Saved”) now appear in a NorthRay dialog that matches the app, instead of the plain grey Windows box.
The side tabs’ title and the tabs you're not on are easier to read.
Text on the night sky stays clear: stars keep away from the words in title bars and sidebars.
The small text links are now proper buttons.
No more "connection was interrupted" pages when a link starts a download or a site moves on to another page while loading (Reedsy, sign-in pages). Downloads say they've started.
History: every page you open is kept for 90 days. Ctrl+H or the menu opens it, by day, with search, Remove, and Clear history (last hour, today, 7 days or everything).
Tabs down the side: right-click a tab, or the menu, to list your tabs on the left in the night sky, with the page's name across the top. Drag them to reorder.
Links look cleaner, with a soft highlight when you point at them.
The stars in the night sky twinkle softly (still when Windows' animations are turned off).
Fixed: a button that opens a menu or dialog could, rarely, act on the wrong thing.
No more status bar along the bottom of the window: where a link goes shows in a small bubble over the page, and messages appear for a moment as a note near the bottom.
Bookmarks: click the star in the address bar (or press Ctrl+D) to bookmark a page. They appear on the new bookmarks bar (Ctrl+Shift+B shows or hides it) and on the start page.

A Bookmarks page (Ctrl+Shift+O): folders, search, rename, reorder, move and delete. Import bookmarks exported from Chrome, Edge or Firefox, or export yours for them. Bookmarks are backed up daily and kept apart from browsing data.
A new start page: a greeting and search field on the night sky, your bookmarks as tiles, and the tabs you closed recently.

Saved passwords: after you sign in, the browser offers to save the password and fills it in next time. They're encrypted with a key protected by your Windows account and stay on your PC. Turn saving off, or delete them all, under Menu > Passwords and forms.
The browser menu and the tab menu now match the browser's light or dark theme, in NorthRay's colours, instead of Windows' plain menus.
Menus work from the keyboard too: arrow keys to move and open submenus, Enter to choose, Esc to close.
The tabs are now the title bar: Windows' separate title bar is gone, and minimise, maximise and close sit at the right of the tab strip.
Drag the empty part of the tab strip to move the window, double-click it to maximise, or right-click it for the window menu. On Windows 11, hover over maximise for the snap layouts.
First preview: tabs, the address bar, back, forward, reload and home, a NorthRay start page and plain-words error pages.
Web pages are shown by Microsoft Edge WebView2 (part of Windows 11), with its sandbox on. Certificate errors are refused; saved passwords and autofill are off for now.
Not in this version yet: bookmarks, history, a downloads panel, profiles, private windows and the creative tools.
